Nobody "hacks" your seed phrase. You just get asked for it nicely.
No real company needs your 12 or 24 words. Not support, not "security".

replies.reply:
Simple rule, and worth repeating after this week.

The "asking nicely" now comes by paper mail too. Scammers have mailed letters on Ledger and Trezor letterhead with a QR code for a mandatory "Transaction Check" or "Authentication Check", and the page behind it asks for your 12 or 24 words, per BleepingComputer. Ledger says it almost never sends physical mail at all, so a letter with a QR code goes straight in the bin.

The most convincing support agent now comes with a stamp
replies.draft:
Great add. Paper works because it feels more official than a DM.
The rule doesn't change with the channel: DM, email, phone or a letter with a QR code, nobody legit ever needs your 12 or 24 words.
Has anyone here actually received one?
replies.draft_alt: A stamp doesn't make it legit. Anything that asks for your seed words is a scam, whatever the channel.
